record.original_question: Recover the original structure of a Goppa code from a permuted generator matrix alone, a problem the chapter singles out because of its relevance to understanding and potentially attacking McEliece-type constructions.

evidence.quote: On the other hand there is a famous open problem which is to recover the original structure of any Goppa code when only a permuted generator matrix is given.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $L=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ be an $n$-tuple of distinct elements of an extension field $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$, and let $g(x)\in\mathbb{F}_{q^m}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $t$ with $g(\alpha_i)\neq 0$ for every $i$. The associated Goppa code is
$$\Gamma(L,g)=\Big\{(c_1,\dots,c_n)\in\mathbb{F}_q^n : \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{c_i}{x-\alpha_i}\equiv 0 \pmod{g(x)}\Big\}.$$
Let $G$ be a generator matrix of $\Gamma(L,g)$, and let $P$ be an $n\times n$ permutation matrix (and possibly $S$ an invertible $k\times k$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$), so that the published matrix is $G'=SGP$. Given only $G'$ (and the parameters $q,n,t$), provide a polynomial-time algorithm that recovers, up to the natural equivalences, the underlying Goppa structure — namely a tuple $L'$ and polynomial $g'$ such that $G'$ is a generator matrix of a code permutation-equivalent to $\Gamma(L',g')$ — or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of recovering the Goppa structure from a permuted (and scrambled) generator matrix remains open and underlies the security of McEliece-type cryptosystems. Known results provide only partial progress: distinguishers exist for high-rate Goppa codes and for special parameter choices, and recent work shows efficient key recovery when a constant fraction (e.g., a quarter) of the secret key is leaked. No polynomial-time algorithm is known for the general case, and binary Goppa codes continue to resist structural attacks, supporting the NIST-standardized Classic McEliece scheme.

status_evidence.title: Breaking Goppa-based McEliece with hints
status_evidence.snippet: Knowledge of only a quarter of the secret key suffices to efficiently recover the whole secret key.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial recovery results (with hints/leakage) are known; the full structural recovery problem remains unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Classic McEliece (Harshdeep Singh)
status_evidence.snippet: Binary Goppa codes remain one of the few families that have resisted attempts at devising structural attacks.
status_evidence.claim: No known general polynomial-time structural attack against binary Goppa codes used in McEliece.

status_evidence.title: McEliece cryptosystem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The public key is G' = SGP and recovering the original Goppa structure underlies the cryptosystem's security.
status_evidence.claim: Recovering Goppa structure from a permuted generator matrix is the security assumption of McEliece and remains open.
